tools.name: ping
tools.description:
Checks that this MCP server is reachable and reports its version.

Use this only to diagnose connection problems. It returns no course data.

tools.name: seminars_search
tools.description:
Finds seminars in the IT-Schulungen.com catalogue.

Use this first when a topic is known but the seminar identifier is not.
The search is semantic and covers the whole seminar text, so describe the
goal in the customer's own words -- "wie sichere ich unsere
Container-Umgebung ab" finds Docker and Kubernetes security seminars that
share no word with the question. A keyword list works worse than a
sentence. Results come back by relevance.

Two operators exist: a phrase in double quotes, and a term prefixed with
a minus sign to exclude it. Either one turns the search back into a
keyword match, so use them only to correct a search that went wide.

Each record carries `topics`, the subjects the seminar is tagged with --
use them to say why a seminar fits and to tell close candidates apart.

Each record also carries `prices`, one per delivery form: the amount and
what it is per, nothing more. What is included and what costs extra --
an exam voucher, catering on site -- comes only from `seminar_get`, so
call it before stating what a seminar costs in total; until then say
"from". All amounts are net, plus VAT. When the
delivery form is not known, lead with the open seminar, priced per
participant; name the in-house price per day only when a team or company
is asking or there is no open seminar, and coaching or a subscription
only when asked. A price without an amount is price on request, and so
is a seminar without `prices`.

Returns a compact record per seminar, each with `url`: the page on
IT-Schulungen.com. Enquiries and bookings do not run through this server,
so that link is where a customer has to go -- name it whenever a seminar
is recommended, exactly as returned: its query string is part of the
link. Call `seminar_get` with a `guid` from this list for the
agenda and prerequisites, and `seminar_dates` for scheduled dates.

query.description: What the seminar should be about, at least 2 characters

topic.description: Exact topic name or identifier from `seminar_topics`

tools.name: seminar_get
tools.description:
Returns one seminar with its description, agenda and prerequisites.

The texts are markdown. Prices come along in full, one per delivery form
with what is included and what costs extra -- the only place that says
so; `seminars_search` carries the amounts alone.

`url` is the seminar's page on IT-Schulungen.com and the place to send a
customer: this server answers questions, it does not take enquiries or
bookings. Hand it on exactly as returned, query string included. If the
field is missing, fall back to the portal's own search
rather than guessing an address.

A seminar carries one price per delivery form, not one price: an open
seminar is priced per participant, an in-house seminar and a coaching per
day. All amounts are net, plus VAT. Always name which form a price
belongs to, and read `calculation_unit` before stating an amount.
`offer_type` says how far the price commits: `not-binding-inquiry` is a
starting point for an enquiry, not a quote.

tools.name: seminar_dates
tools.description:
Lists the scheduled dates of a seminar, soonest first.

Past dates are never returned. Without `from` the window starts today.
`from` and `to` are calendar days in German time, and both are included.
An empty result means nothing is currently scheduled -- it does not mean
the seminar does not exist.

Each date carries the cities it runs in; a city of type `virtual` is an
online delivery, `place` is on site. Dates that are cancelled, postponed
or already over are never returned.

`status` is what to lead with when suggesting a date:

  guaranteed  this seminar runs, whatever else happens -- recommend these
              first, and say so, because it is the customer's strongest
              reason to pick one date over another
  planned     scheduled and open for enrolment, not yet confirmed to run

`direct_booking` appears only on dates that can be booked straight
through the portal, with `direct_booking_until` as the last day for it.
**Its absence says nothing about availability.** Every date listed here
can be enquired about and enrolled in; direct booking is a shortcut, not
a condition. Never tell a customer a date is unavailable because this
field is missing.

`seminar` names the course the dates belong to -- name, duration and
its `url` -- so the list can be presented under that heading. It is
left out only when the lookup failed; the dates still stand.

`begin` and `finish`, per date and per day in `days`, are UTC. The
seminars run in local time (Europe/Berlin; Vienna and Zurich are the
same zone): convert before quoting a time, so 07:00Z is 09:00 in summer
and 08:00 in winter, never "7 Uhr".

from.description: Earliest start date, "YYYY-MM-DD". Defaults to today

city.description: Place name such as "München", or "online" for virtual delivery

tools.name: seminar_topics
tools.description:
Searches the topic vocabulary seminars are tagged with.

Use this to turn a customer's wording into a filter value for
`seminars_search`, and to check whether a product or technology is
covered at all. Aliases are searched too, so "K8s" finds "Kubernetes" and
"AKS" finds "Azure Kubernetes Services".

This is a filter axis, not a catalogue: a hit means the topic exists, not
that a seminar on it does. `seminars_search` answers that.

query.description: Part of a topic name or alias, e.g. "Kubernetes"

type.description: One of manufacturer, topic, technology, software, software_version, audience

tools.name: seminar_locations
tools.description:
Lists the places seminars are held at.

The catalogue runs in a fixed set of cities, plus a virtual classroom for
online delivery. Use this to answer "where do you teach this?" and to
check a place before passing it to `seminar_dates` -- a city that is not
in this list has no dates, however the customer spells it.

query.description: Part of a place name, e.g. "Frank"

tools.name: seminar_difficulties
tools.description:
Lists the difficulty levels a seminar can be filtered by.

Call this before passing `difficulty` to `seminars_search`; the filter
takes an identifier, not a label.
